title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). We work over a base S with a 'special' marked curve X. The pieces are:
- the open curve X, whose points at infinity are indexed by a finite set I;
- its compactification X^ (the hat);
- the normalization Y of X^, a proper smooth (possibly disconnected) curve;
- the set A of double points, and its set of preimages Ã in Y (the half-edges, with an involution σ).
Then X^ = Y/σ_Ã, meaning Y with the paired points of Ã glued, and X = (Y \ I)/σ_Ã. The dual graph has vertices S (the components), edges A, half-edges Ã and legs I. The structure map I → S sends each marked point to the component carrying it.

Problem being served. The notes study the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν}, that is, the stratification of the boundary of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification and the 'tranches' (tubular slices) along strata. One wants to describe how a curve pinned by a graph G yields curves pinned by smaller graphs. This is needed to see how the boundary strata and their 'bords de la tranche' fit together.

The operation on the previous page:
- choose A' ⊂ A and I' ⊂ I;
- normalize X^ at the nodes J = A \ A' to get X^';
- delete the points of I \ I'.
The result is the curve X' = X^' \ I'. Its graph is the subgraph with the same vertex set S, edge set A' and legs I'.

This page:
1. The 'complétée' (completed/formal structure) of X' is obtained from that of X. One keeps the same generic specialization (the reading is uncertain; the next page says 'la spécialisation pour G' étant celle pour G'). The map I' → S is induced by I → S.
2. Refinement. On X^' = Y/σ_Ã' there are, besides the marked points I and the double points A', new canonical marked points. These form the set J̃ ⊂ Ã, the preimage of J = A \ A', of cardinality 2·Card(A \ A'). So X^' carries the canonical marked set J̃ ⊔ I.
3. The page breaks off just before the generalization made on the next page. Instead of discarding J̃ and I \ I', one may keep any subset I' ⊂ I ⊔ J̃ as marked points. Then I' → S is given by I → S together with the 'origin' map Ã → S.

Modern summary. Cutting a set of edges of a stable graph turns each cut edge into two legs. Optionally forgetting some legs then defines a morphism of graphs G → G'. Partial normalization gives the corresponding map from G-pinned curves to G'-pinned curves. This is the inverse of Knudsen's clutching morphisms. It is also exactly the 'cutting edges' morphisms in the graph categories underlying modular operads.
errors: No mathematical error. One unflagged gap: if legs or half-edges are discarded, the resulting marked curve need not be stable (or even 'special' in the required sense) without a stabilization or contraction step. Grothendieck does not address this here; it may be harmless for his class of 'courbes spéciales' over the tranche.

Minor point: the edges of the subgraph are A', and J̃ is to be read as a set of half-edges that become legs. The text is consistent on this, but the vertex set S is kept even if some component loses all its special points.

ideas.what: Partial normalization of a nodal marked curve at a subset of nodes, with preimages of the cut nodes becoming new marked points (2 per node); corresponding operation on the dual graph (same vertices, edge subset A', legs I ⊔ J̃)
ideas.modern_name: inverse of clutching/gluing morphisms; boundary strata maps M̄_G → ∏_v M̄_{g_v,n_v}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983), Deligne–Mumford (1969); graph formalism by Getzler–Kapranov (1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and boundary 'tranches' only qualitatively.

ideas.what: Allowing the retained marked set to be an arbitrary subset I' ⊂ I ⊔ J̃ (cut edges plus forget legs) as morphisms between pinned graphs
ideas.modern_name: morphisms in the category of stable graphs (edge-cutting / leg-forgetting); modular operad structure

ideas.what: Formal completion (tranche structure) of the derived curve obtained from that of the original by keeping the same generic specialization
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of local (formal) structure of boundary strata with partial normalization
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard deformation theory of nodal curves (Deligne–Mumford)

missed.claim: Grothendieck organizes the boundary geometry of M_{g,ν} through a functorial system of graph morphisms: cut a subset of edges, turn the half-edges into legs, and keep an arbitrary subset of legs. This anticipates the graph-category formalism later used for modular operads and for the boundary combinatorics of M̄_{g,n}. It is a foreshadowing rather than a new result.
missed.quote: on a sur X^', en plus des points marqués indexés par I et des points doubles indexés par A', un ensemble de nouveaux "points marqués", savoir l'image inverse J̃ de J = A \ A', de cardinal égal à 2 Card(A \ A')
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck working with the operadic structure of the boundary well before Getzler–Kapranov. Mathematically it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping step: partial normalization and cutting edges into pairs of legs, a now-standard operation on stable graphs. It has some historical interest as an early, careful formulation, but contains nothing new.
